turns.text: My 5-month-old finishes every bottle and formula is getting expensive. How can I make feeding him more affordable without cutting corners?
Why is formula the main drink until twelve months? I'd like to understand what's in it that other milks don't have.
When can solids start taking some of the load, and how much would that realistically reduce the formula he needs?
If I spoke to a health visitor about the cost, what help or advice would they be able to give?
What do pediatric dietitians say about store-brand formula? Is it really the same as the expensive tins?
A friend buys formula in bulk online and says it's much cheaper. Is that safe to do, and what should I check?
Someone else said I'm probably wasting a lot by making up more than he drinks. How do I judge the right amount at five months?
Money's tight enough that I'm choosing between formula and the electric bill. Are there assistance programs for exactly this?
How will I know he's getting enough? I worry about that as much as the cost.
Can you give me a practical plan — the cheapest safe way to keep him on formula, when to start solids, and where to apply for help?
